Gram-negative cells appear pink because their cell walls differ structurally from those of Gram-positive bacteria. While both types initially take up the purple crystal violet stain, the key difference lies in their peptidoglycan layers and outer membranes. Gram-negative cells have a thin peptidoglycan layer and an outer membrane. When alcohol or acetone is applied as a decolouriser, this structure allows the purple crystal violet-iodine complex to wash out of the cell.

Once the purple stain is removed, a counterstain called safranin is applied. This pink dye enters the now-colorless Gram-negative cells, making them appear pink or red under the microscope. In contrast, Gram-positive cells retain their thick peptidoglycan layer, which traps the purple complex even after decolourising, so they remain purple.

In the example, demand for rice is elastic because the percentage drop in quantity sold (25%) is much larger than the percentage rise in price (10%). This means consumers are very sensitive to price changes; they quickly stop buying rice when it gets more expensive. Because the drop in sales volume is so significant compared to the price hike, the total money made by sellers actually goes down. In simple terms, "elastic" here means buyers have many alternatives or can easily delay purchases, so a small price increase causes a big loss in sales volume.

Cassava must be processed because its raw roots contain cyanogenic glucosides, primarily linamarin. When plant tissue is damaged, these compounds release hydrogen cyanide, a toxic substance. Processing methods like grating, fermenting, sieving, and roasting are essential to mitigate this hazard. Grating breaks the plant cells, allowing the enzyme linamarase to convert linamarin into hydrogen cyanide. Subsequent steps, particularly roasting and sun-drying, drive off or reduce the remaining cyanide levels. Without proper processing, the cyanide content remains dangerously high, potentially exceeding the safety limit of 10 mg per kg. Consuming poorly processed cassava can lead to severe health issues, including konzo, a paralytic disease, especially in communities relying heavily on cassava during food shortages.

Cassava must be processed before it is eaten to reduce the hazard of hydrogen cyanide, which is released when the plant tissue is damaged. This hazard is due to the presence of cyanogenic glucosides, mainly linamarin, in the roots. When the roots are grated, packed into sacks, and left to ferment, the enzyme linamarase can act on linamarin, and the hydrogen cyanide is driven off. Proper processing, such as grating, fermenting, and roasting, helps to minimize the risk of konzo, a paralytic disease, by lowering the cyanide content in the finished flour to a safe reference limit of 10 mg per kg.

[P04] (AGR 203: Cassava processing and cyanide)
Cassava roots contain cyanogenic glucosides, mainly linamarin, which release hydrogen cyanide when the plant tissue is damaged. Processing reduces this hazard. To make garri, peeled roots are grated, packed into sacks and left to ferment for two to four days while water is pressed out; the mash is then sieved and roasted. Grating breaks the cells so that the enzyme linamarase can act on linamarin, and roasting drives off much of the remaining hydrogen cyanide. Sun-drying of thin chips also lowers cyanide content, but more slowly. For this course, a total cyanide content of 10 mg per kg in the finished flour is the reference safety limit. Poorly processed cassava has been linked to konzo, a paralytic disease, in communities that depend heavily on cassava during food shortages.

[P07] (STA 111: Mean, median and mode)
Measures of central tendency summarise a data set with a single typical value. The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The median is the middle value when the data are arranged in order; with an even number of values it is the average of the two middle values. The mode is the value that occurs most often, and a data set may have more than one mode or none. For the quiz scores 4, 7, 7, 9 and 13, the sum is 40, so the mean is 8; the median is 7; and the mode is 7. The mean is sensitive to extreme values, so when a data set contains outliers the median often gives a better picture of a typical value.
